newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs soft in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs soft in thin trading.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended slightly lower in thin trading on Thursday as the market braced itself for a petroleum price rise.
"The market is becalmed, really, because people are waiting to see the extent of the petroleum rise," a trader said.
Junior petroleum minister T.R. Balu was quoted as saying that he recommended a 15-20 percent increase in state-controlled prices of diesel and liquefied petroleum gas to Prime Minister Gujral.

A trader said that the market had factored in a rise of about that amount, "If it is much below 20 percent it will be seen as irresponsible and if it is much more the market won't like that either," a trader said.
Trading will likely lack direction until a decision is taken, traders said.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.51 points down at 78.17, with the premium over the local market at 19.95 percent from 21.11 percent.
Hindalco rose 50 cents to $31.00/$32.00 and Bajaj Auto fell $1.68 to $29.25/$30.75.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index lost 2.03 points, or 1.67 percent, to 119.43, representing a discount to the local market of 2.19 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index added 2.18 points to 65.41 points, a premium of 37.07 percent over the local market.
Korean GDRs have gained support in recent days on the back of a more favourable yen/dollar exchange rate, traders said, sparking a rally in major exporters.
